findings.detail: Earlier question M1-S29-T1 has nearly the same scene: the support team's shared backend MCP server needs a per-developer secret kept out of version control. It also has the same correct action: reference the token as an environment variable in the committed .mcp.json. Option D repeats that question's wrong option B, which puts the server definition into each developer's ~/.claude.json instead of the shared project config.

blind_answer.reason: Project-scoped .mcp.json is committed and shared with the team, and environment variable expansion (${SUPPORT_API_TOKEN}) keeps each person's token out of version control. Option A leaves the server in her personal config, so no teammate gets it. Option C puts a secret into a committed file, and CLAUDE.md does not configure MCP servers anyway. Option D spreads a hardcoded token around.
